title: Asking with ma and question words
summary: Ask yes-or-no and who-what-where questions without moving a single word.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Chinese asks questions in place. A statement becomes a yes-or-no question by adding 吗 ma at the end, and the word order does not budge: 你是学生 nǐ shì xuésheng (you are a student) becomes 你是学生吗? nǐ shì xuésheng ma? You can also ask A-not-A by repeating the verb around its negative: 你是不是学生? nǐ shì bú shì xuésheng? (are you a student?), 他好不好? tā hǎo bù hǎo? (is it good?), 我们走不走? wǒmen zǒu bu zǒu? (shall we go or not?). Both forms are everyday, and the A-not-A form often sounds a bit more engaged.

Question words simply sit where the answer would sit: 谁 shéi (who), 什么 shénme (what), 哪里 nǎlǐ (where), 什么时候 shénme shíhou (when), 为什么 wèi shénme (why), 怎么 zěnme (how), 怎么样 zěnmeyàng (how about), 几 jǐ (how few, for small counts), 多少 duōshao (how many, how much), 哪 nǎ (which). Never add 吗 ma to a question-word question: 你叫什么名字? nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? is right, and a version ending in 吗 ma is not a sentence. To bounce a question back, use 呢 ne: 我六点起，你呢? wǒ liù diǎn qǐ, nǐ ne? (I get up at six, and you?).

body.speaker: A
body.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

body.speaker: B
body.en: Ahead. Who are you looking for?

body.speaker: A
body.zh: 我找王医生。他今天来吗？
body.py: wǒ zhǎo Wáng yīshēng. tā jīntiān lái ma?
body.en: I am looking for Doctor Wang. Is he coming today?

body.speaker: B
body.py: tā shàngwǔ shí diǎn zài zhèr.
body.en: He is here at ten in the morning.

blocks.title: Practise these
body: 你为什么不喜欢这里？ nǐ wèi shénme bù xǐhuan zhèlǐ? — Why do you not like this place?
他们几点吃饭？ tāmen jǐ diǎn chī fàn? — What time do they eat?
这个包多少钱？ zhège bāo duōshao qián? — How much is this bag?
你去不去开会？ nǐ qù bú qù kāi huì? — Are you going to the meeting or not?
谁在门口？ shéi zài ménkǒu? — Who is at the door?
周末你做什么？ zhōumò nǐ zuò shénme? — What do you do on the weekend?
我请你看电影，怎么样？ wǒ qǐng nǐ kàn diànyǐng, zěnmeyàng? — Let me take you to a film, how about that?

blocks.body: Independent, unofficial practice material written from scratch for general learners of Mandarin. It teaches questions with ma and with question words, and nothing in it is taken from, copied from, or aligned to any commercial course, textbook brand, app, or official exam. It is not an answer key for any test.
